    Mark, this will be a brief report on this morning’s status conference with the court.

    The receiver, Jack Harris, along with his legal counsel, began with a summary of the interim report they filed yesterday (previously submitted to you).

    They mentioned that they had hoped to work with Stantec for the IRRM engineering work, but Stantec was too expensive and conservative.     I noted that we have not seen any of the documents, such as plans, and contracts, and an accounting of the federal funds, and asked that they be given to us. They agreed. Judge Wetzel suggested that the documents be filed on the court clerk site. I anticipate that this will happen in the next two weeks.

    Judge Wetzel said that he would put on an order that no money be released without an application to the court, and a 7-day period in which objections can be asserted.

    He also said that he would hold status conferences, by phone, each month on the last Friday of the month.

    Please let me know if you have any questions about any of this.

At the meeting held at the Woodward in 2022 Judge Wetzel offered 3 options to address the dam . If my recollection is accurate one option which was the least costly was to remove the dam and maintain the stream which would be my preferred option.
The Knox page’s published a story on March 28th. on the dam repairs indicating the removal of 1 tree downstream & 2 upstream as well as removal of vegetation around the spillway . Removal of silt from the lake and replacing the existing spillway drain pipe & installing a new
24-36 pipe .
“The new pipe will integrate with whichever final solution the homeowners choose .”
Keep in mind that these are all interim repairs !
We the homeowners have NOT been shown what options we have at the present time.
If the option to drain the lake and remove the dam is still viable then removing silt is not logical in my opinion since it will have to be filled in again.That is IF that option is still on the table and chosen by the homeowners.
  I and most homeowners want this done and over with yet it’s been dragging on for countless years .
I would like to see the options , have the homeowners vote on the preferred method of repair and work these repairs around that option and not have to do things twice.
They mention that placing the larger pipe now will prevent them from CUTTING INTO THE DAM TWICE” which leads me to believe “THEY “ intend on keeping the dam & lake in place . Is that what the homeowners of 7 & 8 want ?
Yes they said that that the pipe replacement would integrate with any of the options which have yet to be seen.
I would like a clearer vision of what’s going on .
I’m not convinced just because they say so .
Show me and guarantee it.
Marcello Codispoti.

5. The Declarations require all lot owners to become members of the Landings Common Area Association, Inc., which "shall have the sole and exclusive control of the lake located on the land of the Developer and shall be responsible for its care and maintenance."

6. The "lake" includes the Dam.

The Judge did not decide who will have to pay the cost of remediation of the Dam, or ongoing expenses. This will be determined at trial. It is possible that the Judge could find that the homeowners in Phases VII and VIII were required by the Declarations to be members of the Landings Common Area Association, Inc.; which was a mistaken name and should have been The Landings Property Owners Association, Inc., and is therefore changed to that; that the Declarations require the homeowners to pay assessments issued by the corporation for common expenses; that the receiver will issue assessments against each homeowner for the cost of repairing and maintaining the Dam. There are also other possibilities.

Nothing that has happened since that decision by the judge has changed any of the above.

The court appointed a receiver (Jack Harris, of Intercept Management Corp.) on October 4, 2024, and ordered the receiver to do 7 things. Set forth below is a list of those 7 things, and the status of each of them.

I have asked for as much notice as possible in advance of these meetings, so that all who are interested can attend, and this has been promised.
  4. Implement essential risk reduction measures for the maintenance of the Dam. The receiver is working on this, as detailed in the numerous interim reports previously shared with you.

My recommendation to the group is that you all begin right now to determine who among you you would like to be officers in the HOA. That is going to happen before long, and you can get out in front of it now without waiting. You should also be thinking about, and talking among yourselves about, what you would like done with the dam and the lake. Again, there is no need to wait for the court or the receiver to begin that process. And, you can do all of that, which will be necessary anyway, without legal fees.

On September 23, 2024, the court filed a decision on cross-motions for summary judgment, which made a number of findings, but did not resolve the entire case.

Here is a summary of the critical findings made by the Judge.

1. The individual landowners are not the owners of the Dam.

2. The owner of the Dam is The Landings Property Owners Association, Inc.

3. Because The Landings Property Owners Association, Inc. had its articles of incorporation cancelled in 2015, the court is going to appoint a receiver to act on behalf of the corporation. The receiver will be charged with the responsibility to move forward with making a decision on what should be done with the Dam, subject to approval by the Ohio Department of Natural Resources.

4. The residents of Phases VII and VIII are bound by the Declarations which were filed with the County Recorder.

5. The Declarations require all lot owners to become members of the Landings Common Area Association, Inc., which "shall have the sole and exclusive control of the lake located on the land of the Developer and shall be responsible for its care and maintenance."

6. The "lake" includes the Dam.

The Judge did not decide who will have to pay the cost of remediation of the Dam, or ongoing expenses. This will be determined at trial. It is possible that the Judge could find that the homeowners in Phases VII and VIII were required by the Declarations to be members of the Landings Common Area Association, Inc.; which was a mistaken name and should have been The Landings Property Owners Association, Inc., and is therefore changed to that; that the Declarations require the homeowners to pay assessments issued by the corporation for common expenses; that the receiver will issue assessments against each homeowner for the cost of repairing and maintaining the Dam. There are also other possibilities.

Nothing that has happened since that decision by the judge has changed any of the above.

The court appointed a receiver (Jack Harris, of Intercept Management Corp.) on October 4, 2024, and ordered the receiver to do 7 things. Set forth below is a list of those 7 things, and the status of each of them.

1. Secure and encumber available funds for repair and maintenance of the Dam. This has been done.

   2. Seek and obtain public or private financing to complete needed remediation and repairs for the Dam and ongoing maintenance. The receiver is working on this.
   3. Seek input from the Phase VII and Phase VIII Lot Owners as to the design and financing of any construction, remediation, and improvements to the Dam. I have asked for as much notice as possible in advance of these meetings, so that all who are interested can attend, and this has been promised.
   4. Implement essential risk reduction measures for the maintenance of the Dam. The receiver is working on this, as detailed in the numerous interim reports previously shared with you.

Work with Mullins Bros. and the individual lot owners to organize and to establish rules and regulations for the governance and the operations of a HOA and to achieve full compliance with and enforcement of the Declarations of Building and Development Restrictions. We have not yet seen anything from the receiver on this.

Determine needed assessments on the individual lot owners pursuant to the Declarations, and work with the City to implement a mechanism to levy and collect those assessments to finance the design and construction of any remediation and improvements to the Dam. We have not yet seen anything from the receiver on this.

I am expecting that the next few months will see continued work on the essential risk reduction measures for the maintenance of the Dam, and then meetings at the Woodward Opera House about available options for the property.

Mark, this report will give you a status update on our case. Please share this information with our client group. However, it should not be circulated outside the client group, in order to maintain confidentiality and preserve the attorney-client privilege.

On September 23, 2024, the court filed a decision on cross-motions for summary judgment, which made a number of findings, but did not resolve the entire case.

Here is a summary of the critical findings made by the Judge.

1. The individual landowners are not the owners of the Dam.

2. The owner of the Dam is The Landings Property Owners Association, Inc.

3. Because The Landings Property Owners Association, Inc. had its articles of incorporation cancelled in 2015, the court is going to appoint a receiver to act on behalf of the corporation. The receiver will be charged with the responsibility to move forward with making a decision on what should be done with the Dam, subject to approval by the Ohio Department of Natural Resources.

4. The residents of Phases VII and VIII are bound by the Declarations which were filed with the County Recorder.

5. The Declarations require all lot owners to become members of the Landings Common Area Association, Inc., which "shall have the sole and exclusive control of the lake located on the land of the Developer and shall be responsible for its care and maintenance."

6. The "lake" includes the Dam.

The Judge did not decide who will have to pay the cost of remediation of the Dam, or ongoing expenses. This will be determined at trial. It is possible that the Judge could find that the homeowners in Phases VII and VIII were required by the Declarations to be members of the Landings Common Area Association, Inc.; which was a mistaken name and should have been The Landings Property Owners Association, Inc., and is therefore changed to that; that the Declarations require the homeowners to pay assessments issued by the corporation for common expenses; that the receiver will issue assessments against each homeowner for the cost of repairing and maintaining the Dam. There are also other possibilities.

Nothing that has happened since that decision by the judge has changed any of the above.

The court appointed a receiver (Jack Harris, of Intercept Management Corp.) on October 4, 2024, and ordered the receiver to do 7 things. Set forth below is a list of those 7 things, and the status of each of them.

1. Secure and encumber available funds for repair and maintenance of the Dam. This has been done.

  1. Seek and obtain public or private financing to complete needed remediation and repairs for the Dam and ongoing maintenance. The receiver is working on this.
  2. Seek input from the Phase VII and Phase VIII Lot Owners as to the design and financing of any construction, remediation, and improvements to the Dam. The receiver plans to hold several meetings with residents, at the Woodward Opera House, to discuss a “dry” vs. “wet” basis for use with the dam, a decision on final solution course of action, and development of a plan to pay for the debt service which will be incurred in order to finance the construction, as well as ongoing maintenance. I have asked for as much notice as possible in advance of these meetings, so that all who are interested can attend, and this has been promised.
  3. Implement essential risk reduction measures for the maintenance of the Dam. The receiver is working on this, as detailed in the numerous interim reports previously shared with you.
  4. Reinstate the corporation, The Landings Property Owners Association, Inc. This has been done. The receiver is also to establish governance for the operation of the corporation. We have not yet seen anything from the receiver on this.
  5. Work with Mullins Bros. and the individual lot owners to organize and to establish rules and regulations for the governance and the operations of a HOA and to achieve full compliance with and enforcement of the Declarations of Building and Development Restrictions. 4. The residents of Phases VII and VIII are bound by the Declarations which were filed with the County Recorder.

5. The Declarations require all lot owners to become members of the Landings Common Area Association, Inc., which "shall have the sole and exclusive control of the lake located on the land of the Developer and shall be responsible for its care and maintenance."

Mark, this report will give you a status update on our case. Please share this information with our client group. However, it should not be circulated outside the client group, in order to maintain confidentiality and preserve the attorney-client privilege.

On September 23, 2024, the court filed a decision on cross-motions for summary judgment, which made a number of findings, but did not resolve the entire case.

Here is a summary of the critical findings made by the Judge.

1. The individual landowners are not the owners of the Dam.

2. The owner of the Dam is The Landings Property Owners Association, Inc.

3. Because The Landings Property Owners Association, Inc. had its articles of incorporation cancelled in 2015, the court is going to appoint a receiver to act on behalf of the corporation. The receiver will be charged with the responsibility to move forward with making a decision on what should be done with the Dam, subject to approval by the Ohio Department of Natural Resources.

4. The residents of Phases VII and VIII are bound by the Declarations which were filed with the County Recorder.

5. The Declarations require all lot owners to become members of the Landings Common Area Association, Inc., which "shall have the sole and exclusive control of the lake located on the land of the Developer and shall be responsible for its care and maintenance."

6. The "lake" includes the Dam.

The Judge did not decide who will have to pay the cost of remediation of the Dam, or ongoing expenses. This will be determined at trial. It is possible that the Judge could find that the homeowners in Phases VII and VIII were required by the Declarations to be members of the Landings Common Area Association, Inc.; which was a mistaken name and should have been The Landings Property Owners Association, Inc., and is therefore changed to that; that the Declarations require the homeowners to pay assessments issued by the corporation for common expenses; that the receiver will issue assessments against each homeowner for the cost of repairing and maintaining the Dam. There are also other possibilities.

Nothing that has happened since that decision by the judge has changed any of the above.

The court appointed a receiver (Jack Harris, of Intercept Management Corp.) on October 4, 2024, and ordered the receiver to do 7 things. Set forth below is a list of those 7 things, and the status of each of them.

1. Secure and encumber available funds for repair and maintenance of the Dam. This has been done.

   2. Seek and obtain public or private financing to complete needed remediation and repairs for the Dam and ongoing maintenance. The receiver is working on this.
   3. Seek input from the Phase VII and Phase VIII Lot Owners as to the design and financing of any construction, remediation, and improvements to the Dam. The receiver plans to hold several meetings with residents, at the Woodward Opera House, to discuss a “dry” vs. “wet” basis for use with the dam, a decision on final solution course of action, and development of a plan to pay for the debt service which will be incurred in order to finance the construction, as well as ongoing maintenance. I have asked for as much notice as possible in advance of these meetings, so that all who are interested can attend, and this has been promised.
   4. Implement essential risk reduction measures for the maintenance of the Dam. The receiver is working on this, as detailed in the numerous interim reports previously shared with you.
   5. Reinstate the corporation, The Landings Property Owners Association, Inc. This has been done. The receiver is also to establish governance for the operation of the corporation. We have not yet seen anything from the receiver on this.
   6. Work with Mullins Bros. and the individual lot owners to organize and to establish rules and regulations for the governance and the operations of a HOA and to achieve full compliance with and enforcement of the Declarations of Building and Development Restrictions. We have not yet seen anything from the receiver on this.
   7. Determine needed assessments on the individual lot owners pursuant to the Declarations, and work with the City to implement a mechanism to levy and collect those assessments to finance the design and construction of any remediation and improvements to the Dam. We have not yet seen anything from the receiver on this.

The court ordered that all legal counsel participate in monthly telephone status conferences on the last Friday of the month, at 1:00 p.m. The receiver is also required to submit a written interim report before each of these status conferences. To date, these conferences have focused on the receiver’s progress on the risk reduction measures for the maintenance of the Dam. The next conference will take place on June 27, and I will send you a copy of the receiver’s interim report, and highlight the discussion in the conference.

I am expecting that the next few months will see continued work on the essential risk reduction measures for the maintenance of the Dam, and then meetings at the Woodward Opera House about available options for the property.

Please let me know if you have any comments or questions about any of this.

Thank you for your ongoing efforts as the liaison for the group.

Steve

subject: Follow up re: Withdrawal / Substitution of Parties [ES-LEGAL.FID2347402]
bodyText:
In follow up to Mr. Williams' latest email, below is further explanation of how a request to substitute parties based on the sale of a property involved in this lawsuit is handled.

If any of you which are named in this lawsuit would sell your property, as mentioned before, this DOES NOT remove you as a party to the litigation. That said, you are free to terminate our legal services, and we can prepare a motion asking the court to relieve our firm from further representing you, but you are still defendants and third-party defendants. That means that you are still subject to an adverse finding by the court. You are free to stop being part of the group benefitting from our legal services, and paying our fees. But, again, that does not remove you as a party from the case, any more than the sale of the property does.

However, in the past, in similar situations, we have filed motions to substitute parties, where we ask that the buyers be substituted as defendants and third-party defendants for the sellers. Mullins formerly agreed to this, but no longer does. The court has granted each of those motions. We charge $750 to the seller for the preparation and filing of the legal papers, because this is not something to be borne by all of the other property owners. This is the reason for the separate retainer payment of $750 as it is not charged to the group, but only the individual seller(s) that it involves.

Additionally, the purpose of needing the names and contact information for the buyers, as well as a copy of the deed post-closing, is that we need to provide that information to the court with the motion when we ask for the substitution. Once that is granted by the court and the buyers are substituted in as parties to the litigation, they will then need to decide whether they want legal representation, and who that will be.

Please let me know if you have any other questions.

Juli

subject: Dam Litigation Status Conference
bodyText:
This will be a brief report on today's status conference with the court. I participated, and Mark Long was on the call as well.

The main topic of discussion was the Receiver's motion asking for approval to proceed with the Two Pond Option.

Prior to the conference, I filed an opposing memorandum, a copy of which is attached to this email. I expressed concern about the Receiver's opinion that there will quite possibly be unforeseen conditions in the excavation work, which would lead to a change order and additional expense. His motion sought to have this group responsible for all of those added expenses, which he then said today could be as much as $200,000. I argued that the Single Pond option could be done for hundreds of thousands of dollars under the available federal funds, and was therefore preferred by our group.

After lengthy discussion about the two options, the court began to focus on the relative safety of the options, in terms of potential flooding. He decided that he wants to hear from the engineers who had presented the report. He has ordered the Receiver to file a supplemental report by next Friday, which will address the engineer's opinions about flood risk with each of the options, and the cost of financing any potential added expense.

The court is scheduling another telephone conference for some time on the morning of November 12, at which time we will discuss the two options, and the court will then decide what will be done. He has expressed a commitment to moving this process forward to get the work done before the weather turns bad.

If you have any questions or comments, please let me know.

Thank you.

Steve

subject: Dam Litigation Status Report
bodyText:
Today the court held a telephone conference to consider the question of whether to proceed with the Two Pond Option (more expensive) or the Single Pond Option.

Some of you were able to join the call, thank you for participating.

I argued that the court should go with the Single Pond Option. But, the court decided to bless the Two Pond Option, relying on comments made by the engineer, AK Hydro, in the Memorandum I circulated to you the other day.

We can expect to see a formal order from the court shortly, which I will forward.

We will hope now that the contractor can complete the work for the contract price, and will not encounter any unforeseen underground conditions which would justify an increased price through the change order process. If unforeseen circumstances develop, the City will notify the court, and we will have a further telephone conversation about how this should be handled.

I have suggested to the court that the first place to look for funds if this happens is with the balance of funds in the AK Hydro encumbered funds, and the balance of funds in the Receiver's encumbered funds. This will be addressed by the court if we get to that situation.

We will also address later how the ongoing maintenance expenses will be handled.

I will continue to work with Mark Long for our strategy.

Steve Chappelear
